title: Lesson 9 - Pre-implementation readiness: user experience, metrics, and the discovery that prevents rework
description: Prior to an implementation, assess user experience, communication plan, training, and change management, and establish metrics that measure success.

questions.question: Your sponsor asks when success metrics for an Agentforce sales rollout should be defined. What do you advise?
options: After go-live, once real usage data exists
During user acceptance testing, once configuration is frozen
Prior to implementation, with the business, as part of the readiness assessment
Only if the project runs over budget
questions.explanation: Metrics must be set prior to implementation so there is an unbiased baseline, and they are agreed with the business rather than with the build team alone.

questions.question: A sales user keeps forgetting which field to update on the new record page. Which training mechanism puts the instruction where they are already looking?
options: A printed job aid left at the desk
An in-app guidance prompt on the record page
A change set containing the field
questions.explanation: In-app guidance renders on the page the user is viewing, which solves the last mile that classroom training and job aids lose over time.

questions.question: A program has an executive sponsor and a detailed communication plan, yet adoption stalls in week two. Which readiness element was most likely missing?
options: User champions from the most affected group involved in design
questions.explanation: An executive sponsor without user champions from the most affected group involved in design stalls once the sponsor stops repeating the message, which readiness assessment exists to catch.
